```artifact
Use-Cases & User Stories

Use-Case: UC-001 - Set LOW VTI Alarm Threshold
Goal: As a user, I want to set the threshold for the LOW VTI alarm so that it triggers when the VTI for the current breath exceeds the set value.

Primary Flow:
1. User accesses the GUI settings for alarms.
2. User selects the LOW VTI alarm.
3. User inputs a value for the threshold.
4. System validates the input value.
5. System sets the threshold for the LOW VTI alarm to the input value.

Alternative Flow:
1a. User inputs an invalid value (e.g., non-numeric, out of range).
1b. System displays an error message and prompts user to correct the input.

Exception Flow:
1c. System fails to set the threshold due to a technical error.
1d. System displays a system error message and prompts user to try again later.


Use-Case: UC-002 - Trigger LOW VTI Alarm
Goal: As a user, I want the LOW VTI alarm to trigger when the VTI for the current breath exceeds the set threshold.

Primary Flow:
1. User sets a threshold for the LOW VTI alarm.
2. User performs a breath test with a VTI value above the threshold.
3. System computes the VTI for the breath.
4. System activates the LOW VTI alarm.

Alternative Flow:
1a. User performs a breath test with a VTI value equal to or below the threshold.
1b. System does not activate the LOW VTI alarm.

Exception Flow:
1c. System fails to compute the VTI or activate the alarm due to a technical error.
1d. System displays a system error message and prompts user to try again later.


Use-Case: UC-003 - Set HIGH VTI Alarm Threshold
Goal: As a user, I want to set the threshold for the HIGH VTI alarm so that it triggers when the VTI for the current breath exceeds the set value.

Primary Flow:
1. User accesses the GUI settings for alarms.
2. User selects the HIGH VTI alarm.
3. User inputs a value for the threshold.
4. System validates the input value.
5. System sets the threshold for the HIGH VTI alarm to the input value.

Alternative Flow:
1a. User inputs an invalid value (e.g., non-numeric, out of range).
1b. System displays an error message and prompts user to correct the input.

Exception Flow:
1c. System fails to set the threshold due to a technical error.
1d. System displays a system error message and prompts user to try again later.


Use-Case: UC-004 - Trigger HIGH VTI Alarm
Goal: As a user, I want the HIGH VTI alarm to trigger when the VTI for the current breath exceeds the set threshold.

Primary Flow:
1. User sets a threshold for the HIGH VTI alarm.
2. User performs a breath test with a VTI value above the threshold.
3. System computes the VTI for the breath.
4. System activates the HIGH VTI alarm.

Alternative Flow:
1a. User performs a breath test with a VTI value equal to or below the threshold.
1b. System does not activate the HIGH VTI alarm.

Exception Flow:
1c. System fails to compute the VTI or activate the alarm due to a technical error.
1d. System displays a system error message and prompts user to try again later.


Use-Case: UC-005 - Boundary Value Test for LOW VTI Alarm Threshold
Goal: As a user, I want to ensure that the LOW VTI alarm threshold works correctly at the boundary values.

Primary Flow:
1. User sets the LOW VTI alarm threshold to the minimum possible value.
2. User sets the LOW VTI alarm threshold to the maximum possible value.
3. System validates the input values.
4. System sets the thresholds accordingly.

Alternative Flow:
1a. User sets the LOW VTI alarm threshold slightly below the minimum value.
1b. System displays a warning message and prompts user to reconsider the input.

Exception Flow:
1c. System fails to set the threshold due to a technical error.
1d. System displays a system error message and prompts user to try again later.


Use-Case: UC-006 - Negative Test Case for Invalid LOW VTI Alarm Threshold Input
Goal: As a user, I want to ensure that the system rejects invalid inputs for the LOW VTI alarm threshold.

Primary Flow:
1. User inputs an invalid value (e.g., a negative number, a string).
2. System rejects the input and displays an error message.

Alternative Flow:
1a. User inputs a valid number within the acceptable range.
1b. System sets the threshold to the input value.

Exception Flow:
1c. System fails to reject the invalid input and sets the threshold anyway.
1d. System displays a system error message and prompts user to try again later.
```
